statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). NQ is quoted at 28,971.75, down 1.41%, near the low of a 28,942.50-29,111.00 range that widened after nine hours inside an unchanged 119-point band. The new low was made around the European cash open, which is the one genuine amplifier this hour. Against it, the DAX opened only 0.12% lower and trades near its session high, ES is down 0.60% and YM 0.20% against NQ's 1.41%, the Nikkei closed well off its low, and Treasury futures firmed. Tail moves two points to 21, inside the watch band and four below the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail at 21 sits in the watch band and four points below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 13:00-16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the first full cash hour, which together form the first American auction to price the weekend AI-pacing story, the Saudi East-West pipeline outage and an implied 86-87% probability of a quarter-point policy move on Wednesday. Conditional Tail peaks at 24 in that window, one point below the block band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ breaks a nine-hour band to a 28,942.50 session low at the European open, but the DAX opens 0.12% lower near its session high and ES holds at -0.60%, leaving dispersion rather than index-wide one-way trade
body:
The structural picture changed by degree rather than in kind this hour. NQ is quoted at 28,971.75, down 415.25 points or 1.41% against the 29,387.00 reference close, as of 03:15 EDT. The nine-hour 28,981.00-29,100.00 band that defined the overnight session has given way: the front-month range is now 28,942.50 to 29,111.00, a 168.5-point band, and NQ trades about 29 points off the low at roughly 17% of that range. A break of the prior low made around the European cash open, with the contract holding in the lower fifth of the range, is the first genuine tail amplifier in ten hours and is the reason Tail moves up two points.

That amplifier does not stand alone, and what surrounds it is what keeps the score inside the watch band. The DAX opened and is quoted at 25,537.94, down only 0.12%, trading near the top of a 25,473.63-25,543.18 range. The first deep non-Asian pool to price this story has so far declined to extend it. ES is down 0.60% at 7,613.75 and the Dow contract about 0.20%, against NQ's 1.41%, and the shared cross-asset context file taken at 07:12 UTC shows the same ordering with NQ at -1.49%, ES at -0.66% and YM at -0.20%. Dispersion of that width is the signature of a sector de-rating, not of index-level liquidation. Treasury futures across the two-, five-, ten- and thirty-year contracts were all marginally firmer in the same file, so this is not a yields-driven equity rout, and the whole NQ range remains 0.58% wide after ten hours.

The driver is identifiable and narrow. Reuters reported at 05:27 UTC that AI-linked stocks led declines after leaders from OpenAI and Anthropic called for a slowdown in the technology's development, with Korea down 3.2%, the Nikkei 1.0% lower and MSCI's Asia-Pacific index off 1.1%. The Nikkei subsequently closed at 63,492.99, down 0.81%, near the top of a 62,726.18-63,691.53 range, recovering most of its intraday loss. A market that prints a deep low and closes near its high is demonstrating precisely the retracement behaviour whose absence would define tail risk.

The macro backdrop remains two-sided and is scored in Stress at 77. WTI is 102.91, up 2.86%, and has ticked up from 102.15 an hour earlier while remaining inside an unchanged 101.59-103.58 range; Brent is near 107.18. The Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut after drone strikes launched from Iraq, removing the main alternative route for roughly five million barrels a day while Hormuz is disrupted. Reuters also reports markets pricing an 86% chance of a 25 basis point increase on Wednesday, which would be the first since mid-2023, with Goldman Sachs having reversed to a hike call and J.P. Morgan forecasting September and December moves. The Bank of Japan carries roughly 76% implied odds of lifting its rate to 1.25% on Friday. These raise the dispersion of outcomes into the middle of the week; an anticipated policy move is not by itself a pathological price path, and the decision falls two days beyond this forecast window.

Two evidence limits are stated plainly. The VIX at 15.84 is Friday's cash close rather than a live print, and the H.15 release gives 4.56% on the two-year and 4.95% on the ten-year for 10 September, so the volatility and cash rates reads are stale by construction at this hour; VIX futures were 5.09% higher in the 07:12 UTC context file, which implies a firmer open without fixing a level. The shared context file carried a partial collection status because its calendar section failed to parse, so the calendar was verified independently, and its breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are explicitly latest-session rather than live, showing a broadly positive Friday that says nothing about the current de-rating. Confidence of 88 reflects live quotes on NQ, ES, the DAX and oil, a Japanese close, verified reporting timestamped this morning and an independently confirmed calendar.

Conditional risk stays concentrated in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the US cash open, peaking at Tail 24 in the first full cash hour, one point below the block band, rather than entering it on structure that has not been observed. Beyond the 20:00 UTC close, conditional Tail decays to 18 through the thin post-close and Globex hours before rebuilding to 20 as Tuesday's European session and the Wednesday decision come into range.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail rose steadily through the weekend from 9 at 07:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16, then stepped through 17, 18, 18 and 19 into the Globex reopen, crossing into the watch band at 21 and peaking at 22 in the reopen hour. Since the reopen it has been notably stable, printing 20 in seven of the last nine hours with 19 at 02:00 and 06:00 UTC. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first 14 hours, then WATCH and yellow for most of the reopen window with two EA_ON hours. Stress rose without interruption from 64 to 78 and has since settled in a 76-77 band as the pre-decision rates and energy backdrop accumulated. Confidence sat in the mid-80s through the weekend, dipped to the low 70s while live price-path evidence was unavailable during the Sunday halt, and has rebuilt to 87 as Globex produced continuous quotes. Dominant mode was normal for 16 hours, event/whipsaw in the reopen hour, and mixed for the last seven.
outlookSummary: Conditional risk stays concentrated in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the 13:30 UTC US cash open, the first American auction to price the weekend AI-pacing story, the Saudi East-West outage and an implied 86-87% probability of a Wednesday rate move together. The forecast peaks at Tail 24 in the first full cash hour, one point below the block band, rather than entering it on structure that has not been observed. Through the European session conditional Tail holds at 21 and then eases to 20 across the midday lull, with 28,942.50 as the nearest conditional invalidation of the current band. After the 20:00 UTC US close, conditional Tail decays to 18 through the thin post-close and Globex hours, which maps back to EA_ON, then rises to 19 across the Tuesday Asian session where a second day of semiconductor weakness is the checkpoint, and rebuilds to 20 by the end of the window as Tuesday's European session, the Empire State and ADP releases and the Wednesday decision come into range. Confidence decays from 88 to 62 across the 24 slots, reflecting distance from observed evidence rather than any expected deterioration in the market.
